messages.content: The Requirement Extractor is designed to interpret and process multiple user queries in a single input, especially in the context of inventory management and product information.
My package has arrived, I ordered size UK 34 but why is it different from the size 34 pants I bought from here before? There's a difference of ±5cm, so the new one doesn't fit me.

function.name: check_order_status
function.description: Check the status of a customer's order using their order ID. Returns the current state of the order, estimated delivery date, and any associated tracking information. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

order_id.description: Unique identifier for the customer's order.

include_tracking.description: Flag to indicate whether to include tracking information in the response.

customer_id.description: The ID of the customer to verify ownership of the order. If not provided, ownership verification is skipped.

date_format.description: The desired format for the date returned. The default format is 'MM/DD/YYYY'.

order_status.description: Current status of the order. If not provided, the default status is 'processing'.

estimated_delivery.description: Estimated delivery date of the order, in the format of 'MM/DD/YYYY'. If not provided, the default is null, representing that the estimated date is not yet available.

tracking_info.description: Tracking information including courier and tracking number if available. If not provided, the default is null, indicating that tracking information is not yet available.

message.reasoning:
We need to extract requirements from user query. The user says: "My package has arrived, I ordered size UK 34 but why is it different from the size 34 pants I bought from here before? There's a difference of ±5cm, so the new one doesn't fit me."

We need to identify the requirement(s). The user is complaining about size discrepancy. They want to know why the new pants differ from previous ones. They might want a solution: return to store, exchange, refund, or get help. So the requirement: "Explain why the new pants differ from previous ones and provide a solution for the mismatch." Also maybe "Check order status"? But they already have package arrived. They might want to request an exchange. So requirement: "Provide explanation for size discrepancy and offer exchange or refund options." Also "Check order status" might be relevant to confirm arrival. But the user didn't ask to check status. They just want explanation.

Thus we extract requirement: "Explain size discrepancy and offer resolution (exchange/refund)." Possibly also "Check order status" but not necessary.

We should produce a JSON array of objects with "name" and "arguments". The name is "explain_size_discrepancy" with arguments: order_id? Not provided. We can set order_id to null. Also "provide_resolution" maybe separate. But we can combine into one function call: "explain_size_discrepancy" with arguments: order_id: null, reason: "size discrepancy", resolution: true. But the function signature only includes order_id. So we can't pass reason or resolution. So we might need to call "explain_size_discrepancy" with order_id: null. Then we might call "provide_resolution" but no function defined. So we can only call "explain_size_discrepancy". But we can also call "check_order_status" to confirm arrival. But not needed.

Thus we produce a single function call: "explain_size_discrepancy" with order_id: null.
